title: Compatibility windows, rollback policy, and upgrade assistant for runtime releases
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: We need a concrete, operational policy that combines semantic versioning, LTS channel behavior, defined compatibility windows, explicit rollback criteria, and an automated migration/upgrade assistant for runtime releases. Current guidance is fragmented across playbooks and several RFCs. This ticket consolidates requirements and implements the first-pass automation (migration-checker + canary orchestration) for runtime-2.0 and future LTS channels.

Scope: policy language for what constitutes a breaking change vs allowed patch; definition of a compatibility window (time + metric thresholds) during which opt-in clients get early exposure; rollout gates for canaries and percentage rollouts; automated verifier tooling that runs a client-adapter test matrix; rollback triggers and automated rollback steps; telemetry required for decisioning. Not in scope: language-level SDKs (separate task).
acceptance_criteria: Policy doc published in Confluence and linked from runtime release checklist
Migration-checker CLI v0.1 that validates client API surface vs runtime contract (unit tests + integration run)
Canary pipeline that supports 3-phase rollout (internal-10%-50%-full) with configurable timers and gate thresholds
Rollback automation that can revert a staged rollout to previous LTS within 15 minutes of trigger
Telemetry dashboards show 95th/99th latency, error-rate, and quality-regression signals for each canary cohort
design_decisions: Adopt strict semver for public runtime RPC surface: MAJOR increments permitted only with a documented migration guide and a 90-day compatibility window
Allow MINOR to add backward-compatible features (no client break); MINOR may include opt-in heuristics that require explicit client opt-in headers
PATCH releases are for bug fixes and must not change external request/response schema; enforce via migration-checker

Introduce a compatibility-window concept: new MAJOR or breaking MINOR is released to 'compatibility' channel for 90 days; during this window, automatic translation shims may be enabled for hosted customers
Canary cadence: internal dev org -> partner orgs -> public ramp. Each stage requires telemetry stability for 24h before advancing unless auto-override is approved by oncall
Rollback criteria are signal-driven (see rollout_gates); rollbacks are executed automatically by the rollout-orchestrator unless a manual hold flag is set
rollout_gates: Latency regressions: 95th percentile token latency increase > 7% over baseline for > 30 minutes -> fail gate
Error rate: increase in server-side 5xx rate >= 0.5 percentage points vs baseline for > 10 minutes -> fail gate
Quality regressions: automated eval-suite average BLEU/ROUGE decrease > 2% on primary prompt set for a canary cohort -> fail gate
Cost regression: per-token cost increase > 10% when normalized for traffic mix -> advisory gate (requires PM sign-off)
Resource saturation: GPU memory pressure above 85% for sustained 10 minutes -> fail gate
migration_tooling: migration-checker v0.1 (CLI): compares runtime OpenAPI + contract markers against client adapter expectations; returns actionable diff with suggested shims
rollout-orchestrator: Jenkins/GitHub Actions pipeline snippets + k8s job templates to advance/rollback cohorts
compat-mode header: runtime supports 'X-Redwood-Compat: opt-in' allowing experimental adapters to be exercised during compatibility window
amcli upgrade-advisor integration: surfaces recommended client changes and lines-of-code impact based on telemetry
automated canary validator job (k8s CronJob) that runs smoke-tests and the eval-suite against canary cohort every 15 minutes
